name: Apple Cider Doughnut Baked Oatmeal

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, divided, plus more for greasing the pan

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 350°F. Generously grease an 8- by 8-inch baking pan with butter; set aside. In a small saucepan, bring apple cider to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-high and simmer, stirring occasionally, until cider measures 1/2 cup, about 30 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool slightly (see notes).

Meanwhile, in a medium skillet, melt 4 tablespoons butter over medium heat. Cook, swirling skillet and stirring frequently, until milk solids are golden brown and butter has a nutty aroma, about 6 minutes. Add apple and cook, stirring constantly, until slightly softened, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat and let apple mixture cool for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a large bowl, whisk together half-and-half, applesauce, egg, brown sugar, baking powder, vanilla, salt, nutmeg, cardamom, 7 tablespoons reduced cider, and 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon until well combined. Stir in oats. Reserve 1/3 cup cooled apple mixture, then fold remaining apple mixture into oat mixture. Transfer to prepared baking pan and spread into an even layer. Sprinkle reserved apple mixture evenly over top. Do not wipe skillet clean. Let oat mixture stand at room temperature until slightly thickened, about 15 minutes.

Bake until oatmeal is set, 25 to 30 minutes. Meanwhile, add remaining 1 tablespoon butter and remaining 1 tablespoon reduced cider to reserved skillet. Cook over medium-low heat, whisking constantly, until butter is melted and mixture is combined, about 30 seconds. Remove from heat.

Using a pastry brush, brush cider-butter mixture evenly over warm oatmeal. Let cool for 30 minutes. In a small bowl, stir together granulated sugar and remaining 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon. Sprinkle cinnamon sugar evenly over oatmeal. Slice and serve.

description: This apple cider doughnut baked oatmeal turns a favorite fall treat into a make-ahead breakfast with tender apples and cinnamon sugar.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 2 hr 30 min.

Notes: Granny Smith apples provide tartness and retain some texture after cooking. A sweeter apple, such as Gala or Golden Delicious, can be substituted, though the finished oatmeal will taste sweeter and the apple pieces may soften more.
Old-fashioned rolled oats are essential for the proper texture in the finished baked oats. Quick-cooking oats will absorb the liquid more rapidly and may become mushy, while steel-cut oats require different liquid ratios and a longer cooking time.
Measure the reduced cider by volume rather than relying solely on the cooking time, since the rate of evaporation will vary with the saucepan and burner. If the cider reduces below 1/2 cup, add enough water to return it to the correct volume.
Allow the oatmeal to cool for the full 30 minutes before adding the cinnamon sugar. If the surface is still hot and steamy, the sugar will dissolve instead of forming a distinct doughnut-inspired topping.

Make-ahead and storage: The baked oatmeal can be cooled completely, covered, and refrigerated for up to 5 days, or tightly wrapped and frozen for up to 1 month. Thaw frozen oatmeal overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.
Reheat individual portions in the microwave in 30-second intervals until warmed through. To reheat the entire baked oatmeal, cover the pan with aluminum foil and bake in a 325°F oven until heated through, 15 to 20 minutes.
author: Leah Colins
